exposure: Genital Mycoplasma species (Ureaplasma urealyticum, U. parvum, M. hominis, M. genitalium) colonization status
cohort: The study included 100 pregnant women who presented with a shortened cervix (<= 25 mm) before 34 weeks of gestation at a German Tertiary Perinatal Center between 2017 and 2020.
finding: Pregnant women with a shortened cervix who tested positive for genital Mycoplasma and were treated with antibiotics gave birth at the same gestational age as patients without detected Mycoplasma.
gest_age: Gestational age at examination ranged from 18+4 to 33+3 weeks; median gestational age at birth was 250 days for Ureaplasma-positive and 257 days for Ureaplasma-negative patients.
